### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A02 and A08 averaged about 0.86 hours (median about 0.88, middle half between about 0.79 and 0.94 hours), based on 29 observations; in the later window it averaged about 0.45 hours (median about 0.44, middle half between about 0.41 and 0.49 hours), based on 30 observations — roughly half the earlier level. [TWAIT001]
- The spread of these elapsed times also narrowed, from a standard deviation of about 0.11 hours to about 0.06 hours. [TWAIT001]
- The difference is larger than in about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data, but it rests on only about 30 observations per window out of 200 traces each. [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process. Screening 67 units flags about 0.33 items by chance when nothing has changed, so a single flagged timing item — a halving of the A02–A08 elapsed time resting on about 30 observations per window — is what a stable process typically produces, and it does not directly show any change in ordering, participation or routing. [TWAIT001]
